title: Directed cubic-tree savings yield an eventual 4.89153N full B2 lower bound

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. Let L(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee.leading. Let R(n) be the sum of the monomials in guarantee.remainder.terms, each coefficient times n^exponent*(log2 n)^log_exponent*(log2 log2 n)^loglog_exponent; an empty sum is zero. There exists N such that C_B2(f_n)>=L(n)-R(n) for every integer n>=N. All remainder coefficients are the exact declared constants. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The fixed total norm-one language in family.md, The language at every length. Reject lengths below 16 and invalid irreducibility headers. In the field E given by those headers and the lengths t and m defined there, parse the tm-bit payload z and accept exactly when z raised to the sum of 2^(mj) for 0<=j<t equals 1. Ignore the tail and take an empty witness.","guarantee":{"kind":"eventual_lower_bound","leading":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"100000","numerator":"489153"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"remainder":{"kind":"explicit","terms":[]}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"100000","numerator":"489153"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"At every sufficiently large integer actual input length N, the fixed norm-one language has full B2 circuit complexity at least (489153/100000)N, with zero explicit remainder, unrestricted sharing and repeated pins.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v2"}
